penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Building billing/access-control infrastructure for MCP servers requires real API integration work (Stripe Connect, auth tokens, usage metering) — this is a developer infrastructure product, not a service the factory can automate for customers.

rationale: The buyer is a nameable group — indie devs and small teams commercializing MCP servers — and the gap (no native billing/access-control in the protocol) is real and acknowledged by practitioners. However, building monetization infrastructure for other developers is itself a complex developer infrastructure product (think Stripe for MCP), which is fundamentally not buildable with Claude prompts and a landing page. Operational autonomy is very low because the core value is technical plumbing that each MCP seller must integrate. The market is also extremely early (single launch thread, one YC company), and willingness-to-pay is unproven. Total after penalties is 3.3 — well below validate threshold.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator. The product would be an API gateway + billing layer that MCP server developers embed into their products — requiring authentication systems, usage tracking, Stripe Connect integrations, and ongoing reliability engineering. There is no Claude-prompt-plus-form version of this. The factory cannot build or maintain developer infrastructure middleware. Recommend drop and revisit in 6-12 months when the MCP ecosystem has matured and simpler monetization patterns emerge.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai_min (3 < 6) and operational_autonomy_min (3 < 7). Market is too early and the product is infrastructure-level, not service-level.
